spec: Standalone save cards: which emulators the savefile question can answer for a non-libretro catalogue entry, keyed by the %EMULATOR_…% token the launch command names. This is world knowledge under DESIGN.md's boundary rule — each card names the configuration file that governs the emulator's save tree and the catalogue systems it answers for, with source citations at the revision the arrangement ships; the reading itself is code beside the card (atlas/installations.py), which reads that configuration the way the emulator does and states every degradation as a structured caveat. A card is deliberately thin: what SlotA = 8 means, what an empty path key defaults to, how a configured path templates its region — none of that is on the machine, so it lives as cited code, never as a copied value that could age apart from the binary. A card states no flatpak app id: which app the arrangement installs the emulator as is a property of the INSTALLATION rather than of the save question, so it is stated once in emulator_settings.json (#288) — here it could only be stated for emulators that happen to have a save card, which is how MAME's savestate answer came to refuse a launch it could read. A card may also pin the builds its citations were read at, as the optional builds list — each one the release the deploy names, the upstream revision, the stamp the build itself carries as one string constant, the citation tying the three, and the provenance an answer read under that build carries — which a tripwire holds against the deployed binary, passing where it carries one of their stamps as a whole NUL-delimited constant. More than one build is a card whose emulator answers differently by build, and whose resolver reads which build runs (schema 3: the list replaced schema 2's single build block). Every card states its redirects block: the routes one launch can move the emulator's saves by without its configuration being written — a launch flag, an environment variable or the launch's working directory, each with what it moves and a citation at the card's pinned build carrying its limits — and the provenance of what was searched, which is what backs an empty list.

provenance.source: Dolphin 2609, built from commit f84df020 — the release the shipped binary names in its version strings (components/dolphin/bin/dolphin-emu). GameCube: which device sits in each card slot is [Core] SlotA/SlotB in Dolphin.ini, an EXI device id (EXI_Device.h:25-45 — 1 memory card, 8 GCI folder, 9 AGP, 255 none; registered defaults GCI folder for A, none for B, MainSettings.cpp:133-136). A slot value is read the way TryParse reads it — strtoll in base 0 over the whole value, within the int the device id is (Config.h:90-96, Layer.h:36-43, StringUtil.h:65-102). So 0x9 and 011 are both the AGP, and so is 0b1001, because the deployed builds import the C23 strtoll (__isoc23_strtoll), which reads a 0b prefix; a value that does not parse, or does not fit an int, is the slot's default. Every value first loses one pair of surrounding double quotes, as the ini parse strips them (IniFile.cpp:34, StringUtil.cpp:247-253). An empty MemcardA/BPath defaults to <user>/GC/MemoryCard<A|B>.<region>.raw and an empty GCIFolderA/BPath to <user>/GC/<region>/Card <A|B> (GetMemcardPath MainSettings.cpp:783-790, GetGCIFolderPath :851-857); a configured value of either is a template whose region segment the running disc replaces (:793-835, :860-889), so the answer keeps a <region> hole rather than reading the value literally. A GCI file Dolphin writes is named from the save's own directory entry — makercode-gamecode-filename.gci (GCMemcardDirectory.cpp:53-61) — and one it finds keeps its name, none of it derivable from the content path, so the folder groups are unnamed. Which files are a game's is decided by their header instead: the folder's .gci files are listed, not recursively and with the extension in any case, and a running game is given those whose first four header bytes, the game code, equal the first four characters of its disc's game id (GCMemcardDirectory.cpp:192, FileSearch.h:32-36, FileSearch.cpp:34-55, GCMemcardDirectory.cpp:209, GCMemcard.h:245-246, EXI_DeviceMemoryCard.cpp:173-181). The maker code beside it is not compared, and outside netplay the other games' files are loaded from the folder as well (GCMemcardDirectory.cpp:191, NetPlayConfigLoader.cpp:200), so the answer keeps the game code as a <save_id> hole and states that rule beside it rather than naming a file. A raw card of standard size carries no block suffix (EXI.cpp:123-124 defaults to the 2043-block card; a smaller MemoryCardSize appends one, GetMemcardPath MainSettings.cpp:779-781). Wii: a title's save lives in title/<hi:08x>/<lo:08x>/data below NANDRootPath (NandPaths.cpp:63-71), the title id the one the disc's game partition ticket states (VolumeWii.cpp:270-276). Nothing in the content path spells it, so the answer keeps the whole id, high word included, as the <save_id> hole. Booting a disc creates its title's data directory (ES.cpp:834-874, Boot_BS2Emu.cpp:621), so the answer lists the title directories the NAND already holds beside the hole. The user directory is the emulator's XDG data tree, which the arrangement pins and reroutes with symlinks the answer walks. A GBA cartridge adapter (AGP, slot id 9) loads the cartridge [Core] AgpCartA/BPath names (default empty, MainSettings.cpp:92-93) and, beside it, that path with its extension cut the way SplitPath cuts it (StringUtil.cpp:323-356) and .sav appended; the cartridge's save is as large as that file, 0 where it does not open, and exactly that many bytes are written back to it at shutdown, only where the cut path is not empty (EXI_DeviceAGP.cpp:34-45, :73-85, :107-166) — so a .sav with a size is one battery file every GameCube game run with that configuration writes, and a missing or empty one keeps nothing. Not modelled and stated as such where met: the GBA-integration SavesPath, and the GCIFolder*PathOverride keys a movie or netplay session sets. On EmuDeck the emulator is the org.DolphinEmu.dolphin-emu flatpak (emuDeckDolphin.sh:4-5), so the launch's flatpak variant reads the app's own XDG homes below ~/.var/app; EmuDeck grants every emulator flatpak --filesystem=host (installEmuFP.sh:33), so a configured HOST path stays the host path it names; the sandbox's own spellings still lead into the app's trees (/var/config, /var/data, /var/cache) or, for /app, into its deployed files.

provenance.source: PrimeHack, the Metroid Prime fork of Dolphin, read at shiiion/dolphin 81bfb96 — the revision RetroDECK's component master-230724.27 is built from and the one the Flathub flatpak EmuDeck installs is not (53f53e0). The save shape is Dolphin's, inherited whole, so the same reading serves both and the line numbers here are the fork's own. GameCube: which device sits in each card slot is [Core] SlotA/SlotB in Dolphin.ini, an EXI device id (EXI_Device.h:25-46 — 1 memory card, 8 GCI folder, 9 AGP, 255 none; registered defaults GCI folder for A, none for B, MainSettings.cpp:112-115). A slot value is read the way TryParse reads it — strtoll in base 0 over the whole value, within the int the device id is (Config.h:83-89, Layer.h:30-37, StringUtil.h:75-113). So 0x9 and 011 are both the AGP, and so is 0b1001, because the deployed builds import the C23 strtoll (__isoc23_strtoll), which reads a 0b prefix; a value that does not parse, or does not fit an int, is the slot's default. Every value first loses one pair of surrounding double quotes, as the ini parse strips them (IniFile.cpp:34, StringUtil.cpp:228-234). An empty MemcardA/BPath defaults to <user>/GC/MemoryCard<A|B>.<region>.raw and an empty GCIFolderA/BPath to <user>/GC/<region>/Card <A|B> (GetMemcardPath :635-649, GetGCIFolderPath :704-711); a configured value of either is a template whose region segment the running disc replaces (:652-688, :713-748), so the answer keeps a <region> hole rather than reading the value literally. A GCI file the fork writes is named from the save's own directory entry — makercode-gamecode-filename.gci (GCMemcardDirectory.cpp:54-62) — and one it finds keeps its name, none of it derivable from the content path, so the folder groups are unnamed. Which files are a game's is decided by their header instead, as in Dolphin: the folder's .gci files are listed, not recursively and with the extension in any case, and a running game is given those whose first four header bytes, the game code, equal the first four characters of its disc's game id (GCMemcardDirectory.cpp:193, FileSearch.h:13-15, FileSearch.cpp:42-63, GCMemcardDirectory.cpp:210, GCMemcard.h:246-247, EXI_DeviceMemoryCard.cpp:176-184). The maker code beside it is not compared, and outside netplay the other games' files are loaded from the folder as well (GCMemcardDirectory.cpp:192, NetPlayConfigLoader.cpp:139), so the answer keeps the game code as a <save_id> hole and states that rule beside it rather than naming a file. A raw card of standard size carries no block suffix (EXI.cpp:116-119 defaults to the 2043-block card; a smaller MemoryCardSize appends one, GetMemcardPath :638-640). Wii: a title's save lives in title/<hi:08x>/<lo:08x>/data below NANDRootPath (NandPaths.cpp:49-58 — GetTitlePath composes title/<hi>/<lo> at :49-53 and GetTitleDataPath appends /data at :55-58), the title id the one the disc's game partition ticket states (VolumeWii.cpp:272-278). Nothing in the content path spells it, so the answer keeps the whole id, high word included, as the <save_id> hole. Booting a disc creates its title's data directory (ES.cpp:820-858, Boot_BS2Emu.cpp:598), so the answer lists the title directories the NAND already holds beside the hole. The user directory is the fork's own, and which name that is belongs to the build rather than to the emulator (emulator_settings.json states both, #246). A GBA cartridge adapter (AGP, slot id 9) loads the cartridge [Core] AgpCartA/BPath names (default empty, MainSettings.cpp:71-72) and, beside it, that path with its extension cut the way SplitPath cuts it (StringUtil.cpp:304-335) and .sav appended; the cartridge's save is as large as that file, 0 where it does not open, and exactly that many bytes are written back to it at shutdown (EXI_DeviceAGP.cpp:35-45, :73-85, :107-166) — at this revision even with no cartridge configured, in which case the path written is .sav, relative to the launching process's working directory; the Flathub build writes only where the cut path is not empty, as Dolphin does (EXI_DeviceAGP.cpp:34-45 at 53f53e0). Not modelled and stated as such where met: the GBA-integration SavesPath, and the GCIFolder*PathOverride keys a movie or netplay session sets. On EmuDeck the emulator is the io.github.shiiion.primehack flatpak (emuDeckPrimehack.sh:5-6), so the launch's flatpak variant reads the app's own XDG homes below ~/.var/app — where the fork spells its directory dolphin-emu, not primehack. The Flathub flatpak is a later rebase of the fork (53f53e0), so the same reading answers for it with that build's own line numbers, stated beside the app id.

routes.name: XDG_CONFIG_HOME
routes.citation: On Linux the whole memory stick is $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ppsspp, the value taken as given — neither checked for being absolute nor for being empty — else ~/.config/ppsspp (NativeApp.cpp:473-491), and ppsspp.ini is loaded from its PSP/SYSTEM folder (NativeApp.cpp:504-509). So the saves (PSP/SAVEDATA), the savestates (PSP/PPSSPP_STATE), the configuration and the installed games and homebrew (PSP/GAME) all move, and a fresh stick is created with PPSSPP's defaults (PathUtil.cpp:45-140). The PSP's flash0 ships beside the binary and does not move (NativeApp.cpp:483).

provenance.source: xemu v0.8.136, built from commit fc24584c — the release the shipped binary carries as a whole version string (components/xemu/bin/xemu). xemu keeps xemu.toml under the DATA home, not the config one — the shipped binary takes its base path from SDL_GetPrefPath, which on Linux is $XDG_DATA_HOME/<org>/<app>/, and RetroDECK says the same in its own words while linking a config-tree directory there: 'linking back to original location where component will look', dir_prep "$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/xemu" "$XDG_DATA_HOME/xemu/xemu" (component_prepare.sh:16-17). routes.name: --mlc
routes.citation: --mlc <dir> (short form -m) names the Wii U's internal storage for this launch (LaunchSettings.cpp:64, :149-157, a leading '=' trimmed) and outranks settings.xml's mlc_path (ActiveSettings.cpp:242-252); it lives in the launch settings alone and is never written into settings.xml (CemuConfig.cpp:12-18 is the one writer besides the load). Every save lives in the Wii U's internal storage (MLC), resolved the way the emulator resolves it: an --mlc launch flag, else settings.xml's mlc_path, else mlc01 below Cemu's user data (ActiveSettings.cpp:242-268). A 3DS save lives on the emulated SD: the archive mounts '<sdmc>/Nintendo 3DS/<ID0>/<ID1>/title/' and the per-title save is '<high:08x>/<low:08x>/data/00000001/' below it (archive_source_sd_savedata.cpp:21-29), with ID0 and ID1 compile-time all-zero strings (archive.h:22-24) — so the unit is a directory keyed by the title id, the same <save_id> spelling Cemu's card fills. provenance.source: PCSX2 v2.8.2, the release RetroDECK ships, built from commit fd9d310c (the binary carries the commit's full hash). On Linux the DataRoot is $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/PCSX2 where set, else ~/.config/PCSX2 — both the config side (Pcsx2Config.cpp:2223-2243) — with inis/PCSX2.ini inside; a launch passing -datapath <dir> puts it at <dir>/PCSX2 instead (QtHost.cpp:2216-2221, Pcsx2Config.cpp:2251-2252), which ES-DE's PCSX2 command does not pass. provenance.source: RPCS3 build 20184, commit d5213de6, the revision the shipped binary names. The save tree hangs off the emulated PS3's internal drive, whose host directory vfs.yml states: the key /dev_hdd0/, defaulting to $(EmulatorDir)dev_hdd0/ (vfs_config.h:13). $(EmulatorDir) is itself a key of that file: cfg_vfs::get replaces the token everywhere it appears and ends the resulting path with a separator where it has none (vfs_config.cpp:14-64), and what it replaces the token with is get_emu_dir's answer — the stated value as written, or the emulator's config directory where it is empty (system_utils.cpp:148-152, called at System.cpp:450 and passed at :537). Below the drive, saves are one directory per title id under home/<user>/savedata: the binary carries '/dev_hdd0/home/%08u/savedata/' as a whole string, beside '/dev_hdd0/home/%08d/' and the trophy tree. The user is a runtime selection — Emulator::m_usr initialises to '00000001' (System.h:108) and the user manager changes it — and nothing on disk records which one is current, so the answer states the user homes RPCS3's own GetUserAccounts would list (user_account.cpp:35-66 at d5213de6) and the ones it passes over as skipped, and names the uncertainty besides. That those homes are every one the emulator would list is claimed only where every entry found was decided: an entry left undecided here may be one GetUserAccounts keeps, and where one is, the sentence claims the accounts established here instead. It never says the listing could stop early, because neither kind of undecided entry can stop it — the walk below skips an entry whose stat fails and reads on into the next. A name below home/ whose own stat failed here is stated apart from both where check_user accepts it, because GetUserAccounts reaches it through fs::dir (user_account.cpp:41), a readdir walk that stats every entry and skips the ones whose fstatat fails — 'failed metadata (broken symlink?), ignore and skip to next file', unix_dir::read, File.cpp:2391-2405 — so the emulator's verdict on such a name rests on a stat of its own, and a stat that failed for atlas is not known to fail for it. A name check_user rejects is skipped instead, and established as skipped without any stat: that test reads nothing but the name (system_utils.cpp:61-71, applied at user_account.cpp:49-54), so the emulator passes such a name over whichever way its walk went. Both arrangements wire the first user: RetroDECK links saves/ps3/rpcs3 at dev_hdd0/home/00000001/savedata (component_prepare.sh), EmuDeck the same path from its own saves folder (emuDeckRPCS3.sh:189) and runs the AppImage (emuDeckRPCS3.sh:4-5). A second save location sits outside the per-user tree entirely — '/dev_hdd0/savedata/vmc/', the virtual memory cards for PS1 and PS2 classics, also a whole string in the binary — and it is a directory, so it rides as a group of its own with its file names left open, beside the file-set-spans-roots caveat that says a sync walking only the per-user tree misses it. What is written there and under which names has not been read. config.yml stays unread: it is nested YAML, and nothing this answer needs is in it.

Its sibling append_v4 pushes a separator for an empty component where the left side has a filename (path.cpp:558-561), which composes ux0/user/ and the same savedata path below it — so unlike the stem, this reading does not turn on which of the two a caller compiles, and the id contributes no segment of its own either way. A user-id stated as a null node is not that id at all, and five plain scalars are that node: nothing after the colon, ~, null, Null and NULL, the list IsNullString folds (null.cpp:13-16), asked of every untagged plain scalar (singledocparser.cpp:96-97). The key is read as a std::string and yaml-cpp's string conversion answers a null node with the literal null rather than with an empty one (as_if<std::string, void>, impl.h:145-146, read and run at external/yaml-cpp@2f86d137), so init_home asks gui.users.contains("null") whichever of the five the file writes — a directory listed under that key, by a user.xml stating it or by a name whose stem is it, is the user that record preselects, and its tree carries the id as a segment like any other. That the listing holds a user, recorded or empty, is also not by itself that a launch reopens it: an entry that can end the walk may precede it and the order directory_iterator takes is the directory's own, so the reach stays unestablished and the headline drops. The stem answers for directories the emulator did not write: its own writes stamp an explicit id equal to the directory name (save_user, user_management.cpp:145-158, the attribute at :158) — atlas reads each user.xml the same way, so the users it checks the record against are the ones the emulator would list, and a user.xml it cannot read leaves that check not established rather than decided. Where an entry found here is one that could take that third road, the answer states where the listing can end rather than claiming that every user the emulator would list is stated; the other way an entry goes undecided, a user.xml atlas could not read, ends nothing — load_file decides that one directory and the walk goes on.
